title: File an Escalation
subtitle: Name the blocked task, an owner, and a deadline
scenario: It is SD-1. This hire's run is clean - but the gate's other exit is escalation, and you learn it before you need it. Next week's hire has a blocked task: their background check is still pending. File the escalation so a stuck onboarding gets an owner and a deadline instead of quietly going late.
input: A different hire starting next Monday has a blocked task: the background check is still pending with the vendor. Rule: every escalation names the blocked task, an accountable owner, and a deadline to resolve. Background checks are owned by the People Ops Lead; this one must clear by SD-2 to stay on track.
instructions: Assign the accountable owner for that task.
Set a resolve-by deadline relative to the start date.
Validate to mint the escalation record.

fields.label: Blocked task
fields.explain: Escalate the task that is actually blocked - the pending background check - not a task that already completed.

fields.label: Escalation owner
fields.explain: Background checks are owned by the People Ops Lead; an escalation with no accountable owner is how a start date quietly slips.

fields.label: Resolve by
fields.explain: The deadline must leave margin before the start date; SD-2 keeps the hire on track if the check clears in time.

copilotPrompt: Capture an onboarding escalation: which task is blocked, the accountable owner, and a resolve-by deadline relative to the start date. The blocked task is a pending background check owned by People Ops, due SD-2.
successMessage: Escalation filed. The blocked task now has a named owner and a deadline - not silent lateness.

sections.title: Blocked is not late - yet
sections.body: A blocked task only becomes a missed start date if nobody owns it. Escalation is the difference: it turns a stuck task into an accountable, time-boxed action before day one arrives.

sections.title: Owner and deadline, always
sections.body: Every escalation names who will resolve it and by when. 'Someone is looking into it' is not an escalation; 'People Ops Lead, by SD-2' is.

sections.title: You learn it before you need it
sections.body: This week's hire is clean, so you practice on next week's blocked background check. When a real block hits, the escalation form is already muscle memory.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: An escalation record the package can reference in degraded mode. The medium tier routes this hire's own backordered laptop through here for real.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd raise a ticket naming the blocked item, its owner, and a due date - so a stuck task has a person and a clock, not just a worried feeling.

tools.powerAutomate: create an escalation task with an assignee and due date, notify the owner
tools.zapier: 'Create Ticket' with owner and deadline when a task is blocked
tools.python: open an escalation record {task, owner, resolveBy} and alert the owner

takeaway.heading: Escalation filed
points: You named the blocked task, an accountable owner, and a resolve-by deadline.
An escalation with an owner and a clock is what prevents silent lateness.
The gate's non-ready exit is a real path, not a dead end.
You practiced the form before a real block forced it.
The workflow can now escalate a blocked hire instead of missing the start date.
